title: Boutique capacity tilt & contingent hire protocol — runbook draft
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working runbook for a small/targeted capacity-tilt strategy we can apply when demand is concentrated in premium customers or time-limited events (e.g., product launches, enterprise onboarding waves). It focuses on a lightweight contingent-hire pattern + temporary pricing adjustments and customer credit coordination.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Goal: absorb short-duration token demand spikes without long-term headcount commitments while preserving margin and SLA for core customers.
- Tools: contingent contractors/agency pool, reserved burst credit buckets, short-term slab-ups for dedicated customers, emergency price tilt for on-demand (graceful, opt-in).
- Outcome target: <8 weeks to re-normalize (no permanent FTEs), cost-to-serve uplift capped at +20% on marginal periods.

Context & why we need this:
- Recent EE launches + one big enterprise renewal created concentrated demand that leaks into hosted capacity. Hiring FTEs for those windows is expensive and slow; spot GPU/contractor mix looks better.
- We want an explicit protocol that matches finance guardrails (runway + margin) with product/CS needs.

Primary assumptions (working):
- Average marginal cost per 1M tokens during normal: $X (assume $50 for calc here) — placeholder, tie back to per-route token-cost model (see FIN-2872).
- Marginal cost during peak using contingent-layer: +12–25% depending on GPU spot vs reserved.
- Contingent contracts available within 10 business days for inference ops and infra run (scheduling + remote monitoring).
- Enterprise customer credits can be deferred by up to 30 days if we provide an explicit capacity SLA and temporary uplift fee.

Headcount / contingent mix (proposal):
- Contingent Tier A (Ops engineers for burst): 3 contractors (4–6 weeks) = estimated blended cost $120k/month total fully loaded.
- Contingent Tier B (SRE on-call overlay): 1 contractor (2–4 weeks) = $35k/month pro-rata.
- Internal FTE carry: 1 infra lead + 0.5 product PM (no new hires).

Rough cost table (baseline numbers — to be replaced with per-route unit econ inputs):

Period | Extra contractors | Est marginal token run cost | Est uplift vs baseline
-------|--------------------|---------------------------|----------------------
Week 1 | 3 (A) + 1 (B)       | $65k (1M tokens)          | +18%
Week 2 | 3 (A)               | $55k                      | +12%
Week 3 | 2 (A)               | $40k                      | +8%
Week 4 | 1 (A)               | $22k                      | +4%
Weeks 5+| 0 (contingent)     | normal                     | 0%

Notes on numbers: placeholders. Finance to map to per-GPU run rates (spot/reserved) and contractor engagement terms.

Pricing sensitivity and customer signals (how to tilt prices):
- Soft tilt: for on-demand self-serve traffic, introduce a temporary 10% surcharge on requests that exceed per-account free burst thresholds. Communicate as voluntary priority lane for best latency.
- Hard tilt: for new large customers requesting immediate scale and full SLAs, require either a short-term premium (15–25%) or commit credits/slab purchase (thresholds defined below).
- Pricing rules are opt-in for enterprise: default is to use credits/slab. For non-enterprise, apply a gentle metered surcharge with transparent cost breakdown in billing UI.

Customer credit coordination protocol:
- CS to offer a 90-day discounted slab for customers who pre-purchase burst credits at ~20% off list; finance to reserve 60% of proceeds for capacity procurement.
- Credits used during tilt are marked as ‘priority-burn’ to avoid double-billing on refunds.

Trigger thresholds (operational):
- Trigger A: sustained 95th-percentile route latency > SLA and burst queue depth > 110% for 48h => declare Tier-1 tilt.
- Trigger B: committed customer token consumption > 150% of forecasted month projection => notify finance + CS for contract-level mitigation.
- Trigger C: daily hosted token incidence > +40% vs 7-day rolling baseline => consider soft tilt for on-demand.

Decision tree (short):
1) Detection (alerts from observability).
2) Triage (eng-oncall + infra lead assess capacity vs SLAs).
3) If Trigger A or B: stand up contingent hires (contact pool), notify finance (approve up to $200k contingency).
4) Simultaneously present customers with slab/credit option and pricing tilt (CS run).
5) After 2 weeks, reassess usage — ramp down contractors if burn normalizes.
6) Post-mortem, update baseline forecasts and reprice if necessary.

Operational checklist for finance ops (quick):
- [ ] Confirm contractor rates + legal terms (SOW template FIN-SOW-BURST).
- [ ] Pre-approve contingency budget tranche (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Ensure billing UI flags eligible customers and shows transparent surcharge wording (collab with product).
- [ ] Tag accounting entries for burst as ‘temporary capacity procurement’ for P&L clarity.

Open questions / unresolved items (TODOs):
- Exact marginal cost per token for each GPU flavor under contingent vs baseline (ask infra for price_matrix_v2).
- Tax/benefit treatment of repeated contractor usage vs hiring — CFO input required.
- Legal SOW caps for data handling in private deployments (privacy/regulatory risk).

Back-of-envelope scenario sensitivity (example):
- Scenario X (short, shallow spike): 1.2M incremental tokens over 10 days. Cost w/out protocol: $70k. Cost w/contingent & soft tilt: $58k + 10% surcharge recovered (~$6k) => net $52k (saves $18k).
- Scenario Y (long, deep spike): 5M incremental tokens over 30 days. Cost w/out protocol: $320k. Cost w/protocol + contingent + slabs: $280k net (depends on customer slab conversion).

Post-incident metrics (what to record):
- additional contractor FTE-weeks used
- marginal token cost during window (per route)
- revenue recovered via surcharge / credits
- SLA incidents avoided (count)
- time-to-normalize (days)

Reference links & tickets:
- Confluence FIN-2872 (pricing unit-econ baseline)
- Jira JIRA-FIN-5123 (burst-capacity funding approval)
- Slack thread #cs-enterprise-launch (link in ticket)

Appendix A: Sample contractor engagement checklist (ops):
- SOW signed, NDA in place
- Access scoped & temporary keys rotated after offboarding
- Monitoring playbook + runbook handed off

Appendix B: Short note on product impact (PM):
- If we introduce a visible surcharge, product must add clear UI messaging and opt-in flows within 48–72 hours of decision. Must be localized for EU customers (VAT considerations).

Last thoughts / editorial: keep this lean and operational. The goal is not to maximize short-term revenue but to create a repeatable, measured protocol that aligns finance risk appetite with CS/product need for reliability during concentrated events.

-- Aisha (draft)
